# `bin/packet-block`

A tool: run it from the root of an instance (or of the kit, for the kit's own tools).
Source: [`bin/packet-block`](../../../bin/packet-block)

## What it says about itself

```text
bin/packet-block PATH "why"                  THE USER'S ACT (LESSONS.md "No packet carries blocked material").
   bin/packet-block --lines REGEX PATH "why"
   bin/packet-block --extract C-NNN "why"
   bin/packet-block --extract-note C-NNN YYYY-MM-DD "why"
   bin/packet-block --list

Adds to data/packet-rules.json, the instance's list of what no worker's packet may carry (bin/_packet.py): PATH (a file
or directory inside the tree, root-relative in the list; one not yet made is blocked with a warning) out of every packet whole, or, with --lines, only the lines of
PATH matching REGEX (case-insensitive). --extract leaves ledger entry C-NNN and its notes out of every bin/claims-extract,
--extract-note only its notes of that date. The hook refuses every orchestrator command or edit that names the list or this
tool (a plain git add / commit / status / diff of the list excepted): what is blocked is the user's, run with `!`.
Each addition is ledgered as the user's (PACKET-BLOCK). An entry is removed by editing the list by hand.
```

## Lessons it cites

- → **No packet carries blocked material**

## Ledger events it writes

- `PACKET-BLOCK`
